title: Becanus and Bellarmine deny first justification from merits
source_text: XXXIX. Ideoque Becanus queritur suos calumniam pati, quasi docerent impii justificationem, & remissionem peccatorum, esse ex meritis, non vero gratuitam: & asserit dispositiones quae praecedunt justificationem, tametsi bona opera sint, non ta-men mereri primam gratiam justificantem, & remissionem peccatorum: & consequen-ter primam justificationem esse mere gratuitam, nec ullo modo deberi nobis ex justitia. In Summa Theologiae Scholasticae, tom. 2. tract. 4. cap. 4. Similiter Bellarminus Re-mnium malae fidei accusat, quod dicat inter Protestantes & Ecclesiam Romanam in controversiam vocari, quid sit id, propter quod Deus hominem in gratiam recipiat? An sit meritum Filii Dei, an inchoata in nobis novitas? Ac proinde agnoscit nos in gratiam non recipi propter meritum ullum quod nobis insit, nec novitatem vitae esse meritoriam nostrae cum Deo reconciliationis. De Just. lib. 2. cap. 2.
pass_a_gloss: And therefore Becanus complains that his own suffer calumny as if they taught that the justification of the ungodly and the remission of sins are from merits, not free: and he asserts that the dispositions which precede justification, although they are good works, yet do not merit the first justifying grace and the remission of sins; and consequently that the first justification is purely free and in no way due to us of justice (Summa Theologiae Scholasticae, volume 2, treatise 4, chapter 4). Likewise Bellarmine accuses Remnius of bad faith for saying that it is made a controversy between Protestants and the Roman Church what that is for which God receives a man into grace—whether it is the merit of the Son of God, or the begun newness in us. And therefore he acknowledges that we are not received into grace because of any merit that is in us, nor is newness of life meritorious of our reconciliation with God (De Justificatione, book 2, chapter 2).
pass_b_english: Becanus: first justifying grace and remission are not from merits; dispositions do not merit them.
Bellarmine: we are not received for any merit in us or for inchoate newness as meritorious reconciliation.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1073.
